items.title: Raymond James Financial reports October 2026 operating data
items.summary: Raymond James Financial disclosed October 2026 operating metrics showing client assets under administration of $1.95 trillion, up 11% year-over-year and 1% from September 2026. Private Client Group assets in fee-based accounts rose 14% year-over-year to $1.17 trillion, while financial assets under management grew 25% year-over-year to $346.4 billion. The company cited strong advisor retention and recruiting, along with market appreciation and net asset inflows, as drivers of growth.

items.title: US GDP grew 4.3 percent in third quarter 2026
items.summary: Real GDP increased at an annual rate of 4.3 percent in the third quarter of 2026, up from 2.2 percent in the second quarter, according to the Bureau of Economic Analysis second estimate. Growth was driven by increases in investment, consumer spending and government spending, partly offset by a decrease in exports and an increase in imports.

items.title: Personal income rose 0.7 percent in October, consumption grew 0.3 percent
items.summary: Personal income increased $201.8 billion, or 0.7 percent at a monthly rate, in October 2026, according to the Bureau of Economic Analysis. Disposable personal income rose $200.5 billion, or 0.8 percent, while personal consumption expenditures increased $63.8 billion, or 0.3 percent. The personal saving rate stood at 4.1 percent of disposable personal income.

items.title: Imperial Oil appoints Jim Burgess as senior vice-president, finance and administration
items.summary: Imperial Oil Limited announced the appointment of J.E. (Jim) Burgess, age 52, as senior vice-president, finance and administration, and controller effective March 1, 2027. Mr. Burgess, currently treasurer, succeeds D.E. (Dan) Lyons, who will retire after 36 years of service with Imperial Oil Limited and Exxon Mobil Corporation.

items.title: Deere reports $1.051 billion fourth-quarter net income, full-year $4.860 billion
items.summary: Deere & Company reported net income of $1.051 billion, or $3.89 per share, for the fourth quarter of 2026, down 1% from $1.065 billion, or $3.93 per share, in the prior-year quarter. For the full year 2026, net income was $4.860 billion, or $17.95 per share, down 3% from $5.027 billion, or $18.50 per share, in 2025. The company forecast net income for 2027 in the range of $4.50 billion to $5.25 billion, which includes an estimated one-time, non-cash pension settlement charge of $0.25 billion to $0.40 billion.

items.title: Alphabet closes C$6 billion Canadian dollar senior notes offering
items.summary: Alphabet Inc. closed an underwritten public offering of C$6 billion in Canadian dollar-denominated senior notes on November 24, 2026. The offering consists of four tranches: C$2 billion of 4.100% notes due 2029, C$1.25 billion of 4.800% notes due 2034, C$1.5 billion of 5.325% notes due 2038, and C$1.25 billion of 6.000% notes due 2066.

items.title: Restaurant Brands International completes $1B senior secured notes offering
items.summary: Restaurant Brands International completed a $1 billion public offering of senior secured notes on November 24, 2026: $500 million of 6.000% notes due 2031 and $500 million of 6.400% notes due 2036. The company used proceeds to repay a portion of outstanding borrowings under its term loan B facility and to pay fees and expenses related to the offering.

items.title: DTE Energy extends credit facilities to 2031 and increases commitments
items.summary: DTE Energy, DTE Electric and DTE Gas each amended their five-year credit agreements on November 18, 2026, extending the termination date by one year to October 22, 2031. DTE Electric increased its aggregate commitments from $1.0B to $1.25B. Following the amendments, aggregate commitments are $1.5B for DTE Energy, $1.25B for DTE Electric and $300M for DTE Gas.

items.title: Qualcomm grants $50M and $15M value creation awards to CEO and CFO
items.summary: Qualcomm's board approved special long-term equity incentive awards on November 20, 2026, granting $50 million in value creation awards to President and CEO Cristiano Amon and $15 million to Executive Vice President and CFO Akash Palkhiwala. The awards are performance-based restricted stock units vesting over five years based on stock price hurdles ranging from $250 to $500, designed to align executive compensation with long-term stockholder value creation and retain both executives during the company's transformation strategy.

items.title: Amgen settles patent litigation with Bristol-Myers Squibb over ABP 206 biosimilar
items.summary: Amgen reached a settlement agreement with Bristol-Myers Squibb, E. R. Squibb & Sons, L.L.C. and Ono Pharmaceutical to resolve U.S. patent litigation relating to ABP 206, Amgen's investigational biosimilar to OPDIVO (nivolumab). The settlement allows Amgen to launch ABP 206 in the United States on October 1, 2028, subject to FDA approval, before the expiration of patents that could have been asserted against the biosimilar. The FDA's Biologics License Application for ABP 206 has been submitted and accepted for review, with agency action expected by the end of 2026.

items.title: Amphenol expands revolving credit facility to $5 billion
items.summary: Amphenol Corporation amended and restated its revolving credit agreement on November 20, 2026, increasing its unsecured revolving credit facility from $3 billion to $5 billion, maturing in November 2031. The company also expanded its commercial paper programs to $5 billion for U.S. notes and $2.5 billion for euro notes, with the facility undrawn at closing.

items.title: Federal Reserve releases discount rate meeting minutes from October
items.summary: The Federal Reserve Board released minutes from its discount rate review meetings held on October 19 and October 28, 2026. The document notes that the Board's process for setting the discount rate is distinct from the Federal Open Market Committee's process for setting the federal funds rate target.

items.title: Analog Devices reports record fiscal 2026 revenue of $15.2 billion, up 38 percent
items.summary: Analog Devices announced fiscal 2026 revenue of $15.2 billion, up 38 percent from $11.0 billion in fiscal 2025, with fourth quarter revenue of $4.37 billion up 42 percent year-over-year. Operating cash flow reached $6.2 billion and free cash flow $5.5 billion in fiscal 2026, while the company returned $5.4 billion to shareholders via dividends and repurchases. For the first quarter of fiscal 2027, the company forecast revenue of $4.4 billion plus or minus $150 million.

items.title: Medtronic reports Q2 fiscal 2027 revenue of $9.4 billion, up 6.5% organically
items.summary: Medtronic plc reported second quarter fiscal 2027 revenue of $9.364 billion, up 4.5% as reported and 6.5% on an organic basis, roughly 50 basis points above guidance midpoint. Non-GAAP diluted EPS was $1.34, ahead of guidance by 1 cent. The company completed the separation of its Diabetes Business via exchange offer on October 15, 2026, and reiterated full-year FY27 organic revenue growth guidance of 7.25% to 7.75% and non-GAAP EPS guidance of $5.94 to $6.00 despite the separation.

items.title: Sanofi to acquire Insmed for $175 per share in $41.0 billion cash deal
items.summary: Sanofi agreed to acquire Insmed for $175 per share in cash, representing a total equity value of $41.0 billion, a 46% premium to Insmed's closing share price on November 18, 2026. The acquisition includes two commercialized products—BRINSUPRI, which delivered $1.09 billion in revenue through September 30, 2026, and ARIKAYCE, which generated $433.8 million in 2025—plus a phase 3 pipeline program. Sanofi expects the transaction to be accretive to earnings per share by the end of 2028 and to close in the first half of 2027, subject to Insmed shareholder approval and regulatory clearances.
